## Panel F: SIV counts in splice+ vs splice- cells

Prerequisites: the Figure3 `### combined counts` chunk.

Mean per-cell SIV counts compared between splice+ and splice- cells, to test
whether spliced detection is driven by per-cell SIV depth. `splice+` is any
read whose isoform set contains only spliced isoforms: SS, MS, or SS-MS. SS-MS
is the {SS, MS} set (see `resolve_categories` in functions.R), so the read is
certainly spliced and only its splice count is unresolved; US-SS ({US, SS}) and
`any` leave splice status itself open and stay out. This is the same rule the
splice stage composition in Supp Fig 3 uses. `splice-` is the
remaining infected cells (total > 0). The `total` column is stored as log1p, so
it is back-transformed to raw counts (`expm1`) and shown on a log scale. The
difference reported per sample is mean(splice+) - mean(splice-).

```{r}
input.dir  <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/dataframes/")
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig2/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# --- shared figure style for Panels F-I -------------------------------------
# Helvetica is one of the base-14 PDF fonts, so the default pdf device writes it
# by name without embedding. These ggsave calls must therefore stay on the
# default device: cairo_pdf resolves fonts through fontconfig, which has no
# Helvetica here and would silently substitute DejaVu Sans.
fig_font <- "Helvetica"

theme_supp <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = fig_font) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text       = element_text(size = base_size),
          axis.text        = element_text(colour = "black"),
          panel.spacing    = unit(1.2, "lines"))
}

# Sample names set "in vivo"/"in vitro" in italic and the animal in roman, via
# plotmath: "in vivo (W2)" becomes italic("in vivo")~"(W2)". A name that is not
# in vivo/in vitro (ART) stays fully roman.
sample_expr <- function(x) vapply(x, function(lab) {
  if (grepl("^in (vivo|vitro)", lab)) {
    head <- sub("^(in (?:vivo|vitro)).*$", "\\1", lab)
    tail <- trimws(sub("^in (?:vivo|vitro)", "", lab))
    if (nzchar(tail)) sprintf('italic("%s")~"%s"', head, tail)
    else sprintf('italic("%s")', head)
  } else sprintf('"%s"', lab)
}, character(1))

# Facet strips (Panels G-I) and discrete axes (Panel F) share that rule.
sample_labeller <- as_labeller(sample_expr, default = label_parsed)
scale_x_sample  <- function(...)
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) parse(text = sample_expr(x)), ...)

# D195 = ART, Invitro = in vitro, Pacute and W2 = in vivo, kept as the two
# separate animals and ordered W2 first to match the assembled figure.
samples       <- c("W2", "Pacute", "Invitro", "D195")
sample_labels <- c(W2 = "in vivo (W2)", Pacute = "in vivo (Pacute)",
                   Invitro = "in vitro", D195 = "ART")
sample_levels <- c("in vivo (W2)", "in vivo (Pacute)", "in vitro", "ART")

load_care <- function(sample_name) read.csv(paste0(input.dir, sample_name, "_all.csv"))

splice_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(samples, function(sample_name) {
  df <- load_care(sample_name)
  # D195 has no resolved SS or MS read anywhere, so its table ships without
  # those columns; they are filled in rather than left to drop the sample to
  # all-splice-.
  for (col in c("SS", "MS", "SS.MS")) if (!col %in% colnames(df)) df[[col]] <- 0
  df %>%
    filter(total > 0) %>%
    transmute(
      cellID,
      sample       = factor(sample_labels[sample_name], levels = sample_levels),
      raw_SIV      = expm1(total),                      # total stored as log1p
      splice_group = ifelse(SS > 0 | MS > 0 | SS.MS > 0, "splice+", "splice-"))
}))

splice_summary <- splice_cells %>%
  group_by(sample, splice_group) %>%
  summarise(mean_SIV = mean(raw_SIV),
            sem      = sd(raw_SIV) / sqrt(n()),
            n        = n(), .groups = "drop")
print(splice_summary)

# Difference (splice+ - splice-) and Wilcoxon test where both groups exist.
diff_stats <- splice_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pos = sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
    n_neg = sum(splice_group == "splice-"),
    diff  = mean(raw_SIV[splice_group == "splice+"]) -
            mean(raw_SIV[splice_group == "splice-"]),
    p     = if (n_pos > 0 && n_neg > 0)
              wilcox.test(raw_SIV ~ splice_group)$p.value else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop")
print(diff_stats)

# Difference label sits above each sample's violins.
diff_annot <- splice_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(y = max(raw_SIV), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(diff_stats, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(is.na(diff), "no splice+",
                        sprintf("diff = %.0f\np = %.2g", diff, p)))

splice_colors <- c("splice-" = "orange", "splice+" = "purple")

splice_violin <- ggplot(splice_cells,
                        aes(x = sample, y = raw_SIV, fill = splice_group)) +
  geom_violin(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.8,
              scale = "width", trim = TRUE, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.12,
               outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = diff_annot, aes(x = sample, y = y, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.3, size = 3, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = splice_colors, name = "") +
  scale_x_sample() +
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIV counts per cell (log scale)") +
  theme_supp()

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelF_SIV_counts_splice_groups.pdf"),
       splice_violin, width = 7.5, height = 4.5)
print(splice_violin)
```

## Panel F depth control: is splice+ a host-depth effect?

Panel F compares viral counts between splice+ and splice- cells without
adjusting for how deeply each cell was sequenced. This is the adjusted version:
splice status fitted on viral burden and host library size together, so the
burden coefficient is read at fixed depth and the size coefficient says whether
depth adds anything once burden is in the model.

`care_spliced` in the tier tables is `any(is_siv_splice_category(category))`,
the SS / MS / SS-MS rule Panel F writes out as `SS > 0 | MS > 0 | SS.MS > 0`, so
both call the same cells splice+. Panel F's cells come from the combined
per-sample tables; this fit takes Ca*Re-called cells from the tier tables
instead, because host library size is a per-cell quantity only those carry.
D195 is in Panel F but not here: the samples below are the three the tier tables
are read for throughout.

Prerequisite: Figure3.Rmd's `tier_tables` chunk has written `<sample>_tiers.csv`.
Reads those tables only, so it does not need a compute node.
```{r suppfig2_panelF_depth}
panelFdepth_samples   <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute")
panelFdepth_min_cells <- 10

panelFdepth_tiers <- read_tier_tables(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/"),
                                      panelFdepth_samples)

panelFdepth_tests <- purrr::map_dfr(names(panelFdepth_tiers), function(sample_name) {
  called <- panelFdepth_tiers[[sample_name]] %>% filter(care_UMIs > 0, !is.na(size))
  if (nrow(called) < panelFdepth_min_cells ||
      length(unique(called$care_spliced)) < 2) return(NULL)
  fit <- glm(care_spliced ~ log1p(care_UMIs) + log1p(size),
             data = called, family = binomial())
  coefficients <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  tibble(sample = sample_name, n_cells = nrow(called),
         burden_beta = round(coefficients["log1p(care_UMIs)", 1], 2),
         burden_p    = signif(coefficients["log1p(care_UMIs)", 4], 2),
         size_beta   = round(coefficients["log1p(size)", 1], 2),
         size_p      = signif(coefficients["log1p(size)", 4], 2))
})
cat("\n=== splice+ ~ log(viral UMIs) + log(host library size), Ca*Re-called cells ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(panelFdepth_tests), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Panel G: can a 10X threshold recreate the Ca*Re splice+ list?

Panel F shows splice+ cells carry far more SIV reads than splice- cells. This
panel asks the converse, scoring cells by **10X** SIV expression (mac239 UMIs
from the standard gene-expression assay): if we just thresholded 10X counts,
would we recover the cells that Ca*Re splice+/- identifies? 10X has far fewer
reads and carries no splice information, so this asks whether plain SIV
expression depth can stand in for the Ca*Re splice+ call. The label is Ca*Re
splice+ -- an SS, MS or SS-MS read, the same rule as Panel F -- and Ca*Re
total is scored alongside 10X as the best-case reference. The joint
dataframes (Figure 3's after-joining tables) carry both `TenX` (log1p mac239
UMIs) and the Ca*Re splice columns per cell, except SS-MS, which the joint
builder drops and which is read back from the Ca*Re filtered table the
builder itself reads. Universe = **SIV+ cells** (Ca*Re total > 0): the
evaluation is restricted to infected cells, so the no-skill baseline is the
splice+ prevalence among SIV+ cells (Pacute 0.12, W2 0.28, in vitro 0.51).

ART is omitted, and not for want of splice+ cells -- it has 19, every one of
them called on SS-MS. It is omitted because the score under test does not
exist there: not one of D195's 39 Ca*Re SIV+ cells carries a single 10X SIV
UMI (only 3 cells in the whole 8089-cell sample do, none of them SIV+ by
Ca*Re). A 10X cutoff on a score that is identically zero is undefined --
every cell ties, so AUC and AP carry no information, the recall ceiling is 0,
and the top-X% universe (10X > 0) of Panels H and I is empty. The print below
records this.

Both scores are summarised threshold-independently by **AUC** = P(a random
splice+ cell scores higher than a random splice- cell); 0.5 = no information,
1 = perfect. **AP** (average precision) is the area under the precision-recall
curve, whose no-skill baseline is the splice+ prevalence rather than 0.5.

A hard limit: a positive 10X threshold can only flag cells with 10X > 0, so the
maximum recall any 10X cutoff can reach is the fraction of splice+ cells that
are 10X-detected (the `recall_ceiling` below).

The open circle on each 10X curve is the max-F1 cutoff: the 10X threshold that
best balances precision and recall against the Ca*Re splice+ label (F1 = the
harmonic mean of the two). It is the best a supervised 10X cutoff can do, and is
the "optimal cutoff" rule carried into Panel H.

Prerequisite: run Panel F (defines the shared `theme_supp` and
`sample_labeller` used by Panels G-I); otherwise nothing beyond the joint
dataframes and the Ca*Re filtered tables
(`Figure1/CaRe/<group>/bamsort/reads/minimum/`) on disk.

```{r}
joint.dir  <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/joint/dataframes/")
# The joint tables carry SS and MS but not SS-MS: Figure1.Rmd's joint builder
# selects only cellID/CaRe/US/SS/MS out of the Ca*Re filtered table. SS-MS is
# read back from that same file so the label here is the whole spliced set
# under the identical Ca*Re minimums the joint CaRe counts already use.
# combined/dataframes is deliberately not the source: its categories pool 10X
# and Ca*Re molecules, which would leak the score under test into the label.
care.dir   <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/CaRe/")
care.group <- c(Pacute = "viremia", W2 = "viremia", Invitro = "invitro",
                D195 = "ART")
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig2/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Classifier scoring helpers, shared with Panels H and G below.

# AUC via the Mann-Whitney U relationship (handles ties through ranks).
auc_value <- function(score, pos) {
  r <- rank(score)
  n_pos <- sum(pos); n_neg <- sum(!pos)
  (sum(r[pos]) - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2) / (n_pos * n_neg)
}

# PR points: precision (PPV) vs recall (sensitivity), keeping the score cutoff
# that produced each point so operating points can be read back as thresholds.
pr_points <- function(score, pos) {
  ths <- sort(unique(score), decreasing = TRUE)
  df <- data.frame(
    cutoff_reads = ths,
    recall    = vapply(ths, function(t) sum(score >= t & pos) / sum(pos), numeric(1)),
    precision = vapply(ths, function(t) {
      pred <- score >= t
      tp <- sum(pred & pos); fp <- sum(pred & !pos)
      if (tp + fp == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fp)
    }, numeric(1)))
  df[!is.na(df$precision), ]
}

# Average precision: area under the PR curve (rectangle sum over recall steps).
average_precision <- function(score, pos) {
  pr <- pr_points(score, pos)
  pr <- pr[order(pr$recall), ]
  sum(diff(c(0, pr$recall)) * pr$precision)
}

# Read the score cutoff at chosen operating points. Recall rises as the cutoff
# drops, so for a target recall take the strictest (highest) cutoff that still
# reaches it.
cutoff_at_recall <- function(score, pos, target) {
  pr <- pr_points(score, pos)
  ok <- pr[pr$recall >= target, ]
  ok[which.max(ok$cutoff_reads), c("cutoff_reads", "recall", "precision")]
}

# F1 over all thresholds, with the precision and recall behind each value.
f1_curve <- function(score, pos) {
  P <- sum(pos)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(score)), function(t) {
    tp <- sum(score >= t & pos); fp <- sum(score >= t & !pos)
    prec <- if (tp + fp == 0) 0 else tp / (tp + fp); rec <- tp / P
    data.frame(cutoff = t, precision = prec, recall = rec,
               f1 = if (prec + rec == 0) 0 else 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec))
  }))
}

# W2 and Pacute = in vivo (the two animals kept apart), Invitro = in vitro
# (ART omitted: its 10X SIV score is identically zero over its SIV+ cells, so
# there is nothing to threshold -- quantified in the print below, not a claim
# that it lacks splice+ cells).

joint_samples <- c(W2 = "in vivo (W2)", Pacute = "in vivo (Pacute)",
                   Invitro = "in vitro")

# Per-cell SS-MS counts from the Ca*Re filtered table. The joint table's SS and
# MS reproduce this file exactly over the SIV+ universe, so joining SS-MS back
# on is consistent by construction.
read_ssms <- function(sample_name) {
  f <- read.csv(paste0(care.dir, care.group[[sample_name]],
                       "/bamsort/reads/minimum/", sample_name,
                       "_CaRe_filtered.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  names(f) <- make.names(names(f))          # "SS-MS" -> "SS.MS"
  if (!"SS.MS" %in% names(f)) f$SS.MS <- 0
  f[, c("cellID", "SS.MS")]
}

# Load all cells (the _all.csv tables are already 0-filled); restricted to SIV+
# cells just below so the evaluation universe is infected cells. splice+ is
# SS, MS or SS-MS, the same rule as Panel F: SS-MS is the {SS, MS} set, so the
# read is certainly spliced and only its splice count is unresolved. The joint
# SS/MS are stored log1p and SS.MS is a raw count, but > 0 means the same in
# either scale.
tenx_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(names(joint_samples), function(sample_name) {
  read.csv(paste0(joint.dir, sample_name, "_all.csv")) %>%
    left_join(read_ssms(sample_name), by = "cellID") %>%
    mutate(across(c(GEX, CaRe, SS, MS, SS.MS), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x))) %>%
    transmute(
      cellID,
      sample       = factor(joint_samples[sample_name], levels = unname(joint_samples)),
      tenx_SIV      = expm1(GEX),                  # 10X mac239 UMIs (stored log1p)
      care_SIV     = expm1(CaRe),               # Ca*Re total (stored log1p)
      splice_group = ifelse(SS > 0 | MS > 0 | SS.MS > 0, "splice+", "splice-"))
}))

# Restrict to SIV+ cells (Ca*Re total > 0): the evaluation universe is infected
# cells, so the no-skill baseline is splice+/SIV+ (Pacute 0.12, W2 0.28, in
# vitro 0.51), matching the displayed PR baselines and TP/FP ceilings in
# Panels G/H/I.
tenx_cells <- tenx_cells %>% filter(care_SIV > 0)

# Why ART is not one of the samples above: within its Ca*Re SIV+ cells the 10X
# score has no non-zero value, so there is no cutoff to place. It does carry
# splice+ cells under this label, all of them SS-MS, so the count is printed
# alongside to keep the exclusion about the score and not about the label.
art <- read.csv(paste0(joint.dir, "D195_all.csv")) %>%
  left_join(read_ssms("D195"), by = "cellID") %>%
  mutate(across(c(GEX, CaRe, SS, MS, SS.MS), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)))
art_sivpos <- art %>% filter(expm1(CaRe) > 0)
cat(sprintf(paste0("ART (D195) exclusion: %d Ca*Re SIV+ cells, %d of them splice+, ",
                   "of which %d carry any 10X SIV UMI (max 10X = %.0f); %d of all ",
                   "%d cells in the sample are 10X SIV+\n"),
            nrow(art_sivpos),
            sum(with(art_sivpos, SS > 0 | MS > 0 | SS.MS > 0)),
            sum(expm1(art_sivpos$GEX) > 0),
            max(expm1(art_sivpos$GEX)), sum(expm1(art$GEX) > 0), nrow(art)))

# 10X vs Ca*Re as classifiers of the same splice+ label, plus the 10X recall
# ceiling (max recall reachable once 10X-undetected splice+ cells are unreachable).
tenx_summary <- tenx_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    splice_pos     = sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
    prevalence     = mean(splice_group == "splice+"),
    auc_tenx        = auc_value(tenx_SIV,  splice_group == "splice+"),
    auc_care       = auc_value(care_SIV, splice_group == "splice+"),
    ap_tenx         = average_precision(tenx_SIV,  splice_group == "splice+"),
    ap_care        = average_precision(care_SIV, splice_group == "splice+"),
    recall_ceiling = sum(splice_group == "splice+" & tenx_SIV > 0) /
                     sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
    .groups = "drop")
print(tenx_summary)
write.csv(tenx_summary,
          paste0(output.dir, "PanelG_10X_vs_CaRe_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# In-text numbers: average precision of the 10X score against the Ca*Re splice+
# label, one value per sample (the two in vivo animals are scored separately,
# so there is no single in vivo figure).
cat("\n=== Average precision of a 10X SIV cutoff against the Ca*Re splice+ label ===\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tenx_summary))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-16s AP(10X) = %.2f, AP(Ca*Re) = %.2f, splice+ prevalence = %.2f\n",
              as.character(tenx_summary$sample[i]), tenx_summary$ap_tenx[i],
              tenx_summary$ap_care[i], tenx_summary$prevalence[i]))
}

# PR curves for both scores, overlaid per sample.
pr_compare <- tenx_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    pos <- .x$splice_group == "splice+"
    bind_rows(
      cbind(score = "10X",    pr_points(.x$tenx_SIV,  pos)),
      cbind(score = "Ca*Re",  pr_points(.x$care_SIV, pos)))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Supervised optimum on the 10X score (max-F1 cutoff), located with the Ca*Re
# splice+ label; also the reference rule in Panel H.
f1_opt <- tenx_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    f1 <- f1_curve(.x$tenx_SIV, .x$splice_group == "splice+")
    best <- f1[which.max(f1$f1), ]
    data.frame(max_f1 = best$f1, opt_cutoff = best$cutoff,
               opt_precision = best$precision, opt_recall = best$recall)
  }) %>%
  ungroup()
print(f1_opt)

pr_compare_plot <- ggplot(pr_compare, aes(recall, precision, color = score)) +
  geom_hline(data = tenx_summary, aes(yintercept = prevalence),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = f1_opt, aes(opt_recall, opt_precision), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 21, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.9, fill = "white", color = "#2B3990") +
  # Label sits below-left of the point, in the empty area under the curves.
  geom_segment(data = f1_opt, aes(x = opt_recall - 0.03, y = opt_precision - 0.15,
                                  xend = opt_recall, yend = opt_precision - 0.02),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3, color = "#2B3990") +
  geom_text(data = f1_opt, aes(opt_recall - 0.04, opt_precision - 0.17,
                               label = sprintf("max F1 = %.2f", max_f1)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1, size = 3, color = "#2B3990") +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, labeller = sample_labeller) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("10X" = "#2B3990", "Ca*Re" = "#00AEEF")) +
  labs(x = "Recall (splice+ recovered)", y = "Precision (PPV)", color = "Score") +
  theme_supp() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"))

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelG_PR_10X_vs_CaRe.pdf"),
       pr_compare_plot, width = 8, height = 4.5)
print(pr_compare_plot)

# 10X cutoff (mac239 UMIs/cell) at target recalls.
tenx_operating <- tenx_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    pos <- .x$splice_group == "splice+"
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9), function(tr)
      cbind(target_recall = tr, cutoff_at_recall(.x$tenx_SIV, pos, tr))))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()
print(tenx_operating)
write.csv(tenx_operating,
          paste0(output.dir, "PanelG_10X_operating_points.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Top-X% cutoff sweep

The grid of candidate 10X cutoffs both Panel H and Panel I are built on: a
top-X% quantile of the SIV-*expressing* cells (10X > 0), scored against the
Ca*Re splice+ label. Panel H draws these cutoffs on the expression
distribution; Panel I reports what each one costs in false positives.

Prerequisite: run Panel G (defines `tenx_cells`).

```{r}
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig2/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Top-X% sweep over SIV-expressing cells (10X > 0): a lenient cutoff (large X)
# reaches the recall ceiling but at a steep false-positive cost, so TP/FP are
# tracked at each threshold.
pct_grid <- c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 99)

quantile_sweep <- tenx_cells %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    g <- .x$tenx_SIV; pos <- .x$splice_group == "splice+"; nz <- g[g > 0]; P <- sum(pos)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(pct_grid, function(X) {
      cut  <- as.numeric(quantile(nz, 1 - X / 100, type = 1))
      tp   <- sum(g >= cut & pos); fp <- sum(g >= cut & !pos)
      prec <- if (tp + fp == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fp); rec <- tp / P
      data.frame(pct = X, cutoff = cut, tp = tp, fp = fp,
                 precision = prec, recall = rec,
                 f1 = if (is.na(prec) || prec + rec == 0) 0
                      else 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec))
    }))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()
print(quantile_sweep)
write.csv(quantile_sweep, paste0(output.dir, "PanelI_quantile_sweep.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## Panel H: 10X SIV violin with tested cutoffs overlaid

The 10X SIV expression distribution among SIV-expressing cells (10X > 0) — one
violin per sample, using only 10X (no splice label) — with every tested top-X%
cutoff drawn as a rule and labelled at the right of the panel. It shows where
each candidate threshold falls in the expression distribution. The supervised
max-F1 cutoff is the heavy rule, a Ca*Re-derived reference only.

Prerequisite: run Panel G (defines `f1_opt`) and the cutoff sweep above
(defines `quantile_sweep`).

```{r}
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig2/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

tenx_expressing <- tenx_cells %>% filter(tenx_SIV > 0)

# One label per distinct cutoff: at the low end several top-X% quantiles land on
# the same UMI value, so the strictest percentage reaching it carries the label.
cutoff_labels <- quantile_sweep %>%
  group_by(sample, cutoff) %>%
  summarise(pct = min(pct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(pct, "%"))

# Both callouts are drawn once, in the right-hand facet.
last_sample <- levels(tenx_expressing$sample)[nlevels(tenx_expressing$sample)]
opt_annot   <- f1_opt %>% filter(sample == last_sample)
head_annot  <- data.frame(
  sample = factor(last_sample, levels = levels(tenx_expressing$sample)),
  y      = max(tenx_expressing$tenx_SIV) * 2.3,
  label  = "Cutoff at\ntop percentage:")

panelG_plot <- ggplot(tenx_expressing, aes(x = sample, y = tenx_SIV)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = "black", scale = "width", trim = TRUE,
              width = 0.85, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(data = quantile_sweep, aes(yintercept = cutoff), linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_hline(data = f1_opt, aes(yintercept = opt_cutoff), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.16, height = 0, size = 1.1, alpha = 0.8, shape = 16) +
  geom_text_repel(data = cutoff_labels, aes(x = 1.45, y = cutoff, label = label),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, direction = "y", size = 3,
                  segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey50",
                  min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.05, seed = 1,
                  xlim = c(1.45, 2.0)) +
  geom_curve(data = opt_annot, aes(x = 2.15, y = opt_cutoff * 2.6,
                                   xend = 1.95, yend = opt_cutoff),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, curvature = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3,
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.07, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  geom_text(data = opt_annot, aes(x = 2.2, y = opt_cutoff * 3.4,
                                  label = "optimal cutoff\nfrom Ca*Re"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 3, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = head_annot, aes(x = 1.45, y = y, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3, lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, scales = "free_x", labeller = sample_labeller) +
  # Right-hand slack holds the cutoff labels and the two callouts.
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 2.4))) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 1000), labels = c("1", "10", "100", "1000"),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.20))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "10X SIV counts per cell") +
  theme_supp() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelH_10X_violin_cutoffs.pdf"),
       panelG_plot, width = 7.5, height = 5)
print(panelG_plot)
```

## Panel I: the false-positive cost of a 10X cutoff

Panel G used the splice+ label to find the best cutoff; in practice you would
pick a 10X threshold blind. Here we sweep a top-X% cutoff over the
SIV-*expressing* cells (10X > 0) and track true vs false positives at each. A
lenient cutoff (large X) reaches the recall ceiling but accumulates false
positives fast, because the 10X distribution gives no landmark at the splice+
boundary.

Prerequisite: run the cutoff sweep above (defines `quantile_sweep`).

```{r}
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig2/")

# True vs false positives across the top-X% sweep: TP saturates at the recall
# ceiling while FP keeps climbing as the cutoff loosens.
sweep_long <- quantile_sweep %>%
  select(sample, pct, TP = tp, FP = fp) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(TP, FP), names_to = "type", values_to = "count")

tpfp_colors <- c(TP = "#A020F0", FP = "#F5A623")

# The two series are named on the plot instead of in a legend, one label per
# facet, placed off the curves against each facet's own free y scale.
tpfp_labels <- sweep_long %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(ymax = max(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::expand_grid(tibble(type = c("TP", "FP"),
                            label = c("true positives", "false positives"),
                            # TP left-anchored above its curve, FP right-
                            # anchored below its own, so neither runs off the
                            # panel on any of the three free y scales.
                            pct   = c(8, 98),
                            hj    = c(0, 1),
                            yfrac = c(0.95, 0.06))) %>%
  mutate(count = ymax * yfrac)

tpfp_plot <- ggplot(sweep_long, aes(pct, count, color = type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(data = tpfp_labels, aes(label = label, hjust = hj), family = fig_font,
            fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, scales = "free_y", labeller = sample_labeller) +
  scale_color_manual(values = tpfp_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(25, 50, 75, 100)) +
  labs(x = "cutoff at top percentage of 10X SIV+ cells",
       y = "cells called splice+") +
  theme_supp(13) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelI_TP_FP_sweep.pdf"),
       tpfp_plot, width = 8, height = 3.4)
print(tpfp_plot)
```

# Supp Fig 3
## Load: shared settings and tables

Prerequisites: the public-data pipelines under
`submissionScripts/PublicData/` (cellranger, bamsort, process), and the ADT
gate scripts for the CD4 T calls.

```{r load}
min_hiv_reads  <- 2       # HXB2 reads per barcode
hiv_tcell_gate <- TRUE    # CD4 T by ADT protein, by gene where there is no ADT
options(future.globals.maxSize = 8 * 1024^3)  # 8 GiB

public_paths <- list(
  Collora = list(
    counts  = paste0(public.root, "Colloraetal2022/counts"),
    bamsort = paste0(data.root, "Collora/bamsort"),
    rds     = paste0(data.root, "Collora/Seurat/RDS_publishedQC"),
    qc      = list(min_features = 500, max_features = Inf,
                   max_counts = Inf, max_mito = 10),
    hiv_rule = "collora"),
  HIVseq = list(
    counts  = paste0(public.root, "HIVseq/counts"),
    bamsort = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/bamsort"),
    rds     = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/Seurat/RDS_publishedQC"),
    qc      = list(min_features = 500, max_features = Inf,
                   max_counts = Inf, max_mito = 15),
    hiv_rule_published = "frouard"))

# --- SIV tier tables, for Panels B and C -------------------------------------
suppfig3_samples <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute")
suppfig3_tiers   <- read_tier_tables(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/"),
                                     suppfig3_samples)

# --- cNMF usage tables, for Panel B ------------------------------------------
suppfig3_min_cells <- 10
suppfig3_cnmf_integrated <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                                   "combined/cNMF/subpattern/Pacute_W2_integrated_usage_K6.csv")
suppfig3_cnmf_usage <- list(
  Invitro = list(file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                               "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/Invitro_cleaned_usage_K5.csv"),
                 prefix = NULL, labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$Invitro),
  W2      = list(file = suppfig3_cnmf_integrated, prefix = "W2_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels),
  Pacute  = list(file = suppfig3_cnmf_integrated, prefix = "Pacute_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels))

# Usage table for one sample, with the joint run's cell ID tag stripped
suppfig3_cnmf_read <- function(cfg) {
  if (!file.exists(cfg$file)) return(NULL)
  usage <- read.csv(cfg$file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(cfg$prefix)) {
    usage <- usage[grepl(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), rownames(usage)), , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(usage) <- sub(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), "", rownames(usage))
  }
  usage
}

suppfig3_log2FC <- function(tested, reference) {
  log2((mean(tested) + 1e-10) / (mean(reference) + 1e-10))
}

# --- Giron HIV-D pool, for Panel G -------------------------------------------
giron_pools     <- "HIV-D"
giron_care_pool <- c(D_ = "HIV-D")

# --- ART comparison features and levels, for Panel H -------------------------
art_feature_labels <- c(nCount = "host UMIs", nFeature = "host genes",
                        naive_Tcm = "naive/Tcm", Tem = "Tem", cytotoxic = "cytotoxic",
                        Treg = "Treg", cycling = "cycling",
                        OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION = "OxPhos", GLYCOLYSIS = "Glycolysis",
                        MTORC1_SIGNALING = "mTORC1", INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE = "IFN-gamma",
                        INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE = "IFN-alpha",
                        TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB = "TNFA/NFkB",
                        INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE = "Inflammatory",
                        PUBLIC_HIV_UP = "viremic HIV+ signature")
art_features <- names(art_feature_labels)
art_levels   <- c("Giron", "Collora", "HIVseq", "SIV D195", "Human pooled")
```

## Host library size against the viral calls

Prerequisite: the Load chunk above, for `suppfig3_tiers`
```{r suppfig3_depth_confounding}
# Burden bands for the second test, as closed [lower, upper] bounds on Ca*Re
# UMIs per cell
depthconf_burden_bins <- list(c(2, 7), c(8, 31), c(32, Inf))
depthconf_min_cells   <- 10

depthconf_vs_burden <- purrr::map_dfr(names(suppfig3_tiers), function(sample_name) {
  tiers <- suppfig3_tiers[[sample_name]]
  purrr::map_dfr(c(GEX = "GEX", `Ca*Re` = "care"), function(chemistry) {
    called <- tiers[tiers[[paste0(chemistry, "_UMIs")]] > 0, ]
    if (nrow(called) < depthconf_min_cells) return(NULL)
    test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(log1p(called$size),
                                      log1p(called[[paste0(chemistry, "_UMIs")]]),
                                      method = "spearman"))
    tibble(sample = sample_name, n_called = nrow(called),
           rho = round(unname(test$estimate), 3), p = signif(test$p.value, 2))
  }, .id = "chemistry")
})
cat("\n=== Host library size vs viral burden among called cells (Spearman) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(depthconf_vs_burden), row.names = FALSE)

depthconf_gap_by_burden <- purrr::map_dfr(names(suppfig3_tiers), function(sample_name) {
  tiers <- suppfig3_tiers[[sample_name]]
  uninfected <- tiers$size[tiers$tier == "neg"]
  purrr::map_dfr(depthconf_burden_bins, function(bin) {
    called <- tiers$size[tiers$care_UMIs >= bin[1] & tiers$care_UMIs <= bin[2]]
    if (length(called) < depthconf_min_cells) return(NULL)
    tibble(sample = sample_name,
           burden = paste0(bin[1], if (is.finite(bin[2])) paste0("-", bin[2]) else "+"),
           n_cells = length(called),
           median_size = median(called),
           median_size_uninfected = median(uninfected),
           gap_pct = round(100 * (median(called) / median(uninfected) - 1), 1),
           p = signif(suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(called, uninfected)$p.value), 2))
  })
})
cat("\n=== Host library size of called cells vs uninfected, by viral burden ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(depthconf_gap_by_burden), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Panel B: host library size control

Prerequisites: the Load chunk
```{r suppfig3_panelB_hostsize}
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig3/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

panelB_samples <- suppfig3_samples
panelB_bins    <- 10
panelB_ratio   <- 5
# Uninfected is grey because it is a reference, not a chemistry; the two
# infected populations take the figure's method colours
panelB_colors  <- c(uninfected = "grey70", `Ca*Re` = "#00AEEF", `10X` = "#2B3990")
panelB_facets  <- c(Invitro = "in vitro", W2 = "in vivo\n(W2)", Pacute = "in vivo\n(Pacute)")

panelB_host_size <- purrr::map_dfr(panelB_samples, function(sample_name) {
  tiers <- suppfig3_tiers[[sample_name]] %>% filter(!is.na(size))
  bind_rows(
    tiers %>% filter(tier == "neg") %>%
      transmute(sample = sample_name, population = "uninfected", size),
    tiers %>% filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs > 0) %>%
      transmute(sample = sample_name, population = "Ca*Re", size),
    tiers %>% filter(tier != "neg", GEX_UMIs > 0) %>%
      transmute(sample = sample_name, population = "10X", size))
}) %>% mutate(sample = factor(sample, panelB_samples),
              population = factor(population, names(panelB_colors)))

panelB_size_plot <- ggplot(panelB_host_size, aes(size, population, fill = population)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = panelB_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left",
             labeller = labeller(sample = panelB_facets)) +
  labs(x = "host UMIs per cell", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))

# Each population against all uninfected cells and against a size-matched draw
panelB_matched <- purrr::map_dfr(panelB_samples, function(sample_name) {
  cfg <- suppfig3_cnmf_usage[[sample_name]]
  usage <- suppfig3_cnmf_read(cfg)
  tiers <- suppfig3_tiers[[sample_name]] %>%
    filter(tier %in% c("both", "CaRe_only", "GEX_only", "neg"),
           cellID %in% rownames(usage), !is.na(size))
  host_size <- setNames(tiers$size, tiers$cellID)
  populations <- list(
    `Ca*Re` = tiers$cellID[tiers$tier != "neg" & tiers$care_UMIs > 0],
    `10X`   = tiers$cellID[tiers$tier != "neg" & tiers$GEX_UMIs > 0])
  negative <- tiers$cellID[tiers$tier == "neg"]
  patterns <- grep("^Pattern_", colnames(usage), value = TRUE)
  purrr::map_dfr(names(populations), function(population) {
    tested <- populations[[population]]
    if (length(tested) < suppfig3_min_cells) return(NULL)
    breaks <- unique(quantile(host_size[c(tested, negative)],
                              seq(0, 1, length.out = panelB_bins + 1)))
    tested_bin   <- cut(host_size[tested],   breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
    negative_bin <- cut(host_size[negative], breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)
    wanted <- table(tested_bin)
    set.seed(1)
    matched <- unlist(lapply(names(wanted), function(b) {
      pool <- negative[which(negative_bin == b)]
      if (!length(pool)) return(character(0))
      pool[sample.int(length(pool), min(length(pool), panelB_ratio * wanted[[b]]))]
    }), use.names = FALSE)
    if (length(matched) < suppfig3_min_cells) return(NULL)
    purrr::map_dfr(patterns, function(pattern) {
      tibble(sample = sample_name, population = population,
             program = cfg$labels[pattern],
             n_cells = length(tested), n_matched = length(matched),
             log2FC_all = suppfig3_log2FC(usage[tested, pattern], usage[negative, pattern]),
             log2FC_matched = suppfig3_log2FC(usage[tested, pattern], usage[matched, pattern]),
             p_value = tier_safe_p(
               wilcox.test(usage[tested, pattern], usage[matched, pattern])$p.value))
    })
  })
}) %>%
  filter(!grepl("contaminant|contamination", program, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) %>% ungroup()

write.csv(panelB_matched, paste0(output.dir, "PanelB_hostSize_matched.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

panelB_limit <- max(abs(c(panelB_matched$log2FC_all, panelB_matched$log2FC_matched))) * 1.08
panelB_matched_plot <- ggplot(panelB_matched %>%
                                mutate(population = factor(population, c("Ca*Re", "10X")),
                                       sample = factor(sample, panelB_samples)),
                              aes(log2FC_all, log2FC_matched, colour = population)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sample), size = 2.1, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = panelB_colors[c("Ca*Re", "10X")], name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Invitro = 16, W2 = 17, Pacute = 15),
                     labels = c("in vitro", "in vivo (W2)", "in vivo (Pacute)"), name = NULL) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-panelB_limit, panelB_limit), ylim = c(-panelB_limit, panelB_limit)) +
  labs(x = "log2FC vs all uninfected cells", y = "log2FC vs host size matched") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"))

panelB_plot <- panelB_size_plot / panelB_matched_plot + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.4))
ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelB_hostSize_control.pdf"), panelB_plot,
       width = 4.6, height = 7.4)
print(panelB_plot)

cat("\n=== Median host UMIs per population, and excess over uninfected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(panelB_host_size %>%
  group_by(sample, population) %>%
  summarize(n_cells = n(), median_size = median(size), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(pct_excess = round(100 * (median_size / median_size[population == "uninfected"] - 1), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Program log2FC against all uninfected and against size-matched cells ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(panelB_matched %>%
  transmute(sample, program, population, n_cells, n_matched,
            log2FC_all = round(log2FC_all, 3), log2FC_matched = round(log2FC_matched, 3),
            shift = round(abs(log2FC_matched - log2FC_all), 3),
            p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
  arrange(sample, program, population)), row.names = FALSE)
```
